clue.text: Courage to go to the bank when cleaned out?

definitions.meaning: nerve or guts, as in 'lose your nerve'

definitions.text: to go to the bank when cleaned out?
definitions.meaning: an emptied glass container is taken to a recycling bank once it has been rinsed out

explanation.surface: Someone needs nerve to face the bank manager when they are broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaned out' suggests being penniless, but it means a container washed out; a BOTTLE BANK is a British street bin for recycling glass. BOTTLE is also British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is informal British slang for nerve or daring.

clue.text: One metal fused into many

indicators.note: metals fused are melted together, so the letters of the following words are melted down and recast

explanation.surface: A single metal has been melted down into a great number of pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fused' rearranges the letters of INTO and MANY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a brittle metallic chemical element, symbol Sb, so it is one particular metal.

clue.text: Patches cuffs

definitions.meaning: a clout is an old word for a patch of cloth or a rag
to cuff is to strike with the hand, the same as to clout someone

explanation.surface: Repair pieces sewn onto shirt cuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouts are archaic patches of cloth and also blows with the hand, both senses of the same verb or noun.

clue.text: Nothing new about her being shown out

indicators.note: the phrase for second-hand goods wraps around the pronoun, so one surrounds the other

parts.note: something second-hand or used is not new at all
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is escorted out of a place where nothing is new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'Nothing new' reads as a dismissive remark but describes second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ushered is to be guided by an attendant, here escorted towards the exit.

clue.text: Summary of the former USSR?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before or earlier
the Commonwealth of Independent States, the CIS, replaced the Soviet Union, so the old union is what came before it

explanation.surface: A question asking for a brief history of the old Soviet Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The USSR was, cryptically, the 'pre-CIS', since the Commonwealth of Independent States succeeded it in 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: A precis is a short written abstract giving the main points of a longer text.

clue.text: 17th-century girl astride a horse

indicators.note: a rider sits astride a horse with legs either side, so the name straddles the other letters

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A young woman from the seventeenth century sitting on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' is the container signal, picturing the girl's name sitting either side of the horse; a cob is a stocky riding horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobean describes the reign of James I of England, 1603-25, so it means early seventeenth-century in style.

clue.text: Unrestricted state of incapacitated kangaroo?

definitions.meaning: a kangaroo moves by leaping, so one unable to do so is left without its leaps

explanation.surface: An injured kangaroo enjoying a curiously unlimited freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as BOUND-LESS: a kangaroo that cannot bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no bounds has no limits, so it is unrestricted.

clue.text: The best stuff available around the East

indicators.note: the packing word goes round the compass letter, so one encloses the other

parts.note: to stuff is to pack tightly, the same as to cram
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: The finest goods on sale are found in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts E inside CRAM, splitting it CR-AM; 'stuff' looks like a noun meaning goods but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream is the finest part of anything, as in the phrase the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Positions assumed by a duettist?

indicators.note: a position assumed by a performer is a pose adopted, hinting that the letters of these words take up a new form

explanation.surface: Poses struck by one of a pair of singers on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed by' rearranges the letters of A DUETTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes are bodily postures or stances, especially poses struck on stage or in ballet.

clue.text: Agent loses fine performer

indicators.note: the agent word drops a letter, so it is taken away

parts.note: a factor is an agent who does business for another
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent drops a client who is a good performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes F from FACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is someone who performs roles on stage or screen.

clue.text: Self-righteous declaration made by black militants

parts.note: a person declaring what they are begins with I'm
pi is informal British for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A smug statement issued by a group of radical activists.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is a schoolboy shortening of 'pious'. 'black militants' looks political, but it refers to Zulu warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a regiment or band of Zulu warriors, hence black fighters in southern Africa.

clue.text: Headquarters of the French vessels

parts.note: de is French for of or of the
pots are vessels for holding things

explanation.surface: French naval headquarters housing their ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships, but it means containers.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a base where supplies or troops are kept, a sort of headquarters.

clue.text: Engaged, that's the outcome about me and a girl

indicators.note: the result word goes around the two pronouns, so it surrounds them

parts.note: the end is the final result or outcome
taken as written
she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone announces an engagement between themselves and a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'Engaged' suggests marriage but means interlocked, like gear teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that are engaged mesh together, so enmeshed means caught up or interlocked.

clue.text: Neckline that may bring forth a whistle

definitions.text: Neckline that may bring forth a whistle

parts.words: Neckline that may bring forth a whistle
parts.note: not the cut of a dress that draws admiring wolf whistles, but a cord worn round the neck from which a whistle hangs

explanation.surface: A plunging neckline that attracts wolf whistles.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord worn round the neck to carry a whistle, knife or badge.

clue.text: Probably time to tuck into sausage pie

indicators.note: the time letter is pushed inside, as food is tucked into a meal
in printing, pie is type jumbled into disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: It is probably time to start eating a sausage pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' rearranges SAUSAGE to AGUESSS order, then 'to tuck into' puts T inside it to give ATAGUESS; pie looks like food but is printer's jargon for jumbled type.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying at a guess means roughly or probably, an estimate rather than a certainty.

clue.text: I shall enter race and end up a wreck!

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the racing word, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a run is a race

explanation.surface: A runner predicts entering a race and collapsing exhausted at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shall enter' puts I inside RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruin is a building or thing that has been wrecked and fallen into decay.

clue.text: Mandatory work for a bookmaker

definitions.meaning: the craft of putting covers on books

explanation.surface: Compulsory duties for someone who takes bets on horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaker' means a maker of books here, not a betting agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A binding agreement is compulsory, and binding is also the craft of fastening pages into covers.

clue.text: I'd take up position some way away

indicators.note: in a down clue taking something up reads it from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: Someone says they would move to a post a good way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take up' turns ID into DI in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is an amount of space between places, as in going some way.

clue.text: A seaman's got in by the book

indicators.note: the sailor phrase is placed inside, as something got in

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is brought aboard, all done according to the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got in' is the container signal; 'by the book' looks like an idiom but 'the book' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is the Book of Psalms, or a book containing them for worship.

clue.text: Mother joins other females making complaints

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
ladies are women

explanation.surface: Mum meets up with other women to share their gripes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' suggests grumbling, but it means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints in a medical sense are ailments or illnesses, which is what maladies are.

clue.text: A note to finish a list of things to be done

definitions.text: list of things to be done

parts.note: G is a musical note
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A memo to complete a to-do list.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a schedule of items to be dealt with, as at a meeting.

clue.text: Many a shipwreck could be bad luck

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so it stands for many

indicators.note: to wreck is to destroy and scatter, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Losing many sailors in a shipwreck is a misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipwreck' is read in two parts: SHIP as fodder and 'wreck' rearranging A and SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident or piece of misfortune.

clue.text: Short study course for university student in form

indicators.note: the two letters sit inside the word for form

parts.note: a mode is a form or manner
L, for learner, stands for a student, as on driving L-plates

explanation.surface: A brief study course designed for university students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U and L inside MODE, splitting it MOD-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A module is a self-contained unit of study within a longer course.

clue.text: Encourage a king to go on the river

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Urging a monarch to take a trip on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a well-known English river flowing through York.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse is to stir up or excite, so it means to encourage a feeling.

clue.text: Not stormy, but quite changeable

indicators.note: weather that is changeable alters, so the letters of the word alter order

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: calm but rather unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changeable' rearranges QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet weather is calm and still, the opposite of stormy.

clue.text: A dog trial produces a champion

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are reworked to produce something new

explanation.surface: A dog show trial results in a winning dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' rearranges the letters of A DOG TRIAL. 'champion' suggests a prize dog but means a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator is a fighter in the Roman arena, and figuratively a champion of a cause.

clue.text: House gets speech from one of the parties

definitions.meaning: in a theatre an actor's remark meant for the audience, the house, alone
a side in a dispute or contest, one of the opposing parties

explanation.surface: The House of Commons hears a speech from one political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests Parliament, but it means a theatre audience; the second reading splits the answer as A SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a line spoken to the audience unheard by other characters, and a side is one party.

clue.text: Looking for scraps?

parts.note: not a hungry animal seeking leftovers, but someone eager to start fights

explanation.surface: A stray dog hunting for leftover food.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose means aggressive and eager to fight, and a scrap is a fight.
